candidates.snippet: ---  ## 1. Background  In our long-context MLA benchmarks, enabling HiCache L2 causes up to 44.6%–66.6% effective throughput loss at an 80% hit rate—revealing that hit-length-dependent overhead severely erodes the expected speedup of prefix caching.  Specifically, given a cache hit rate `r`, only `(1 - r)` of the tokens require new prefill computation (`extend` tokens). candidates.title: [RFC] Context-parallel support for the unified L3 key scheme
candidates.snippet: ## Summary  We propose extending `plan_unified_kv` with an explicit ownership rule for each attention-CP mode, so the unified key scheme (#33651) can lift its `attn_cp_size > 1` guard instead of falling back to rank-suffixed keys. Each mode gets a writer rule: replicated CP elects one writer, LayerSplit CP is keyed like a PP stage, and KV cache sharding has each page's owner write the whole page.
